1. Clinical Psychologists
NOTE: A clinical psychologist must hold a doctoral degree in psychology and be licensed or certified, on the basis of the doctoral degree in psychology, by the state in which he or she practices.

components.label: Identify the type of your doctoral psychology degree (e.g., Ph.D., Ed.D., Psy.D.)

components.content: 2. Psychologists Billing Independently
NOTE: Answer the questions below only if you are a psychologist billing independently.

components.label: a. Do you render services of your own responsibility, free from the administrative control of an employer such as a physician, institution, or agency?
b. Do you treat your own patients?
c. Do you have the right to bill directly, and to collect and retain the fee for your services?
d. Is your private practice located in an institution or other facility?

components.content: If YES to question (d) above, answer questions 1 and 2 below.

components.label: 1. If your private practice is located in an institution or other facility, is your office confined to a separately identified part of the institution/facility that is used solely as your office and cannot be construed as extending throughout the entire institution/facility?
2. If your private practice is located in an institution/facility, do you also render services to patients from outside the institution or facility where your office is located?

components.content: Physical Therapists/Occupational Therapists in Private Practice (PT/OT) ONLY.

components.label: 1. Do you ONLY render PT/OT services in the patients' homes?
2. Do you maintain private office space?
3. Do you own, lease, or rent your private office space?
4. Is this private office space used exclusively for your private practice?
5. Do you provide PT/OT services outside of your office and/or patients' homes?

components.content: If you responded YES to questions 2, 3 or 4 above, report your private office space as a practice location in Section 4B.
